gen-gf-snowburst-one-satoshi: Wide bridges, tall lowercase, plenty of attitude. Snowburst One is best at shouting in stencil cuts, while Satoshi, with its soaring x-height, is best at speaking in single-width strokes.
gen-luckiest-guy-archivo: Luckiest Guy is cheerful and loud, with its mean line set high. Archivo takes over below with outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height, so a long paragraph moves along with an editorial ease.
gen-luckiest-guy-general-sans: General Sans writes with steady pen pressure and an x-height filling the line. Under the loud Luckiest Guy heading, text glides around each bend without a snag, easy going from line to line.
gen-dafont-disorder-fs-supreme: Raw chaos, big lowercase, glyphs scattered well apart across the line. Supreme is best at crisp, heavy-looking lines of text, where Disorder is best at making noise with no pinched joins.
gen-mystery-quest-fs-epilogue: Epilogue draws wire-thin, constant lines with a tall-bodied lowercase. Under the bookish, nostalgic Mystery Quest, paragraphs feel contemporary, curves unclamped and stubby ascenders staying out of the way.
gen-gf-goldman-general-sans: Goldman spreads wide, commanding letters with generous clearance, and its lowercase stands surprisingly big next to the capitals. General Sans brings a smooth, constant-width line that carries the whole pair.
gen-orbitron-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans sets sturdy, tall lowercase with an eye opening to the right. What lingers is Orbitron, minimal and precise, its letters spread far apart along the line with open apertures.
gen-press-start-2p-fs-epilogue: Epilogue reads approachable and curvy, unclamped, a contemporary wire-like monoline with tall-bodied lowercase and stubby ascender tips. Below the fun, retro Press Start 2P, text runs smooth and unhurried.
gen-press-start-2p-fs-merriweather-sans: Fun comes first in Press Start 2P, with big open-looking bowls and letters pinned far apart like cut-outs. Press Start 2P plays; Merriweather Sans keeps words sturdy and large.
gen-righteous-fs-paquito: Paquito is a confident, approachable serif with hardly any step down from caps to lowercase. And under Righteous, with its bent-rod bowls filling the line, a paragraph reads confidently and warmly.
